name: Chiding
overview: Scripture presents chiding as a form of direct and sometimes stern communication addressing wrongdoing or misunderstanding, as seen when Pharaoh questions Abraham for concealing his marriage, highlighting the seriousness of deceit within relationships (Genesis 12:18-19). Similarly, Abimelech confronts Abraham over actions that brought sin upon his kingdom, emphasizing accountability for causing harm to others (Genesis 20:9). Cain's lament to the LORD reveals a recognition of the weight of his iniquity and the consequences of his sin (Genesis 4:13-14). These examples illustrate that chiding serves both to expose faults and to call for repentance, underscoring God's justice and the need for integrity among His people.
